summary: Diagnostic verification of gradient pacing change (Math.pow(rawT, 1.6)) in useScrollGradient. Scrolled the homepage and measured actual computed background-color of [data-testid=app-root] at each of the 11 bg-transparent sections using white/light heading text. Also captured 11 evenly-spaced screenshots top-to-bottom. RESULT: the 1.6 easing exponent is TOO AGGRESSIVE — 3 sections have failing (unreadable) contrast, and 1 is borderline. The 'light zone' now extends visually well past the last section that owns a solid light background, leaking into sections that assume a dark backdrop.

ui_bugs.component: Industries.jsx (section index 6, heading 'Managed IT & cybersecurity built for your industry.')
ui_bugs.issue: White (rgb 255,255,255) heading text sits on gradient bg rgb(210,225,239) at that scroll offset. WCAG contrast ratio = 1.33 :1 — heading is essentially invisible (screenshot confirms it is almost the same tone as the background). REGRESSION caused by Math.pow(rawT, 1.6).

ui_bugs.component: BusinessReality.jsx (heading 'The Business Reality of AI, Automation & Cyber Risk')
ui_bugs.issue: White heading on gradient bg rgb(189,210,231). Contrast 1.55 :1 — fails. REGRESSION.

ui_bugs.component: WhySpecializedIT.jsx (heading 'Same services you expect. A fundamentally different approach.')
ui_bugs.issue: White heading on gradient bg rgb(127,166,202). Contrast 2.56 :1 — fails WCAG AA large (3.0). REGRESSION.

ui_bugs.component: Compliance.jsx (heading 'Compliance that supports growth, not just audits.')
ui_bugs.issue: White heading on gradient bg rgb(84,133,178). Contrast 3.91 :1 — barely passes AA large (3.0) but fails AA normal (4.5). Body text under this heading may be marginal. Borderline regression.

issues: With Math.pow(rawT,1.6), rawT=0.5 -> easedT=0.35 (bg~rgb(112,156,195) medium blue). Previously (linear) rawT=0.5 -> bg was ~rgb(35,78,125) dark navy. So the entire middle third of the page is now noticeably lighter. The 'descent into a hole' pacing improved for the FINAL third only (rawT 0.7 -> 1.0 still darkens smoothly rgb(50,97,146) -> rgb(6,22,43)); the trade-off is the middle third became too light for white-text sections.

evenly_spaced_scroll_stops.bg: rgb(7,25,48)  (note: at y=0 the fixed hero bg dominates, gradient is at rgb(224,235,244) but the reported color is captured from the outermost app-root AFTER hero paints; screenshot 3 clearly shows very light body under the dark navigation)

computed_gradient_data.descent_pacing_assessment: The final third (rawT 0.6 -> 1.0) does darken smoothly (rgb 86,135,179 -> 6,22,43) — that part of the user's ask is achieved. However the darkening is now concentrated so late that sections 6-10 in JSX order (Industries..Compliance), which live at rawT ~0.32-0.59, no longer have the dark backdrop their white text was designed against. Previous linear behaviour reached near-black too early (user's complaint) — the current 1.6 exponent overcorrects and reaches near-black too late.

action_items: REDUCE the easing exponent — Math.pow(rawT, 1.6) is too strong. Recommended: try 1.15-1.25 as a first step, or switch to a piecewise/smoothstep curve that stays light through rawT<=0.22 (end of AIService/IntroStats light-zone) and then transitions to near-linear afterward. Concretely: at BusinessReality (rawT~0.39) the bg needs to already be at least ~rgb(60,110,160) to keep white heading readable — currently it is rgb(189,210,231).

Alternative: shift gradientStops so index 3-4 (deep blues) land earlier. E.g. compress the light-blue stops (indices 1-3) into the 0-15% range so that by 25% scroll the bg is already the mid-blue rgb(100,148,190).
Verify Industries, BusinessReality, WhySpecializedIT after fix — those are the three hard fails. Compliance is borderline; HowItWorks onward are fine.
Do NOT change any section text colors — the fix belongs in the gradient curve, not in the sections (per user note the sections were intentionally not touched this session).
critical_code_review_comments: useScrollGradient reads document.body.scrollHeight on every scroll frame; fine here but consider throttling with rAF if perf becomes a concern on low-end devices.

The gradient color is applied via inline style on the ref element; on route change (e.g. navigating to /resources) the last computed color persists until first scroll on the new page. Not a bug for HomePage (which re-mounts pageRef), but worth noting.

success_rate.frontend: gradient functions but readability regression in 3 sections (Industries, BusinessReality, WhySpecializedIT); 1 borderline (Compliance); 7 sections OK

context_for_next_testing_agent: The gradient easing was Math.pow(rawT, 1.6) at App.js line 91 during this test. Real computed bg values recorded above at each of the 11 downstream bg-transparent sections. If main agent adjusts the exponent or gradientStops, re-run the same measurement script (scroll each section into view, read [data-testid=app-root] backgroundColor, compute contrast vs the section's h2 color) and confirm all 11 sections reach contrast >= 3.0 (AA large) for their white/light heading. Special watch: Industries at scrollY~4800, BusinessReality at ~6500, WhySpecializedIT at ~8000.
rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE: Math.pow(rawT, 1.6) is an ease-IN curve that flattens the first ~60% of the scroll range in the color-lookup domain. At rawT=0.4 the easedT is only 0.22, so the color lookup returns a stop between indices 2-3 (light blue rgb ~150,180,210) instead of index 4 (medium blue rgb 60,110,160). This is fine visually for the light-zone sections that impose their own bg, but the bg-transparent sections (Industries, BusinessReality, WhySpecializedIT) that live in the rawT 0.3-0.5 range use white text and now sit on light blue backgrounds -> contrast collapses to 1.3-2.6:1. REPRO: hard refresh homepage, scroll to any of the three flagged sections, observe white heading nearly invisible against light-blue gradient. MITIGATION: lower easing exponent to ~1.2 OR remap gradientStops so darker colors land at earlier percentages OR add a bg-color hint on those specific sections (least preferred per user instructions).
